rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both orders establish a presidential advisory body, define its study-and-recommendation purpose, direct government-wide cooperation, and then provide agency assistance under section 214 of the 1945 act, including detailed employees who perform functions assigned by the body. The close sequence and unusually specific assistance language go beyond a shared general topic or isolated boilerplate. C06 offers a broader structural analogue involving a council, studies, reports, committees, and agency assistance, while C11 resembles the child's establishment, study, reporting, cooperation, and staffing provisions, but neither matches C03's compact operative sequence as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: All executive departments and administrative agencies of the Federal Government are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Conference and to furnish such information and assistance not inconsistent with law as may reasonably be required in the performance of its functions.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Committee and to furnish it such information and assistance, not inconsistent with law, as it may require in the performance of its duties.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim government-wide cooperation provision, adapted only to the new body's name and minor wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Each executive department and administrative agency which is represented by one or more members of the Conference ... shall ... furnish assistance to the Conference in accordance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945, 59 Stat. 134 (31 U.S.C. 691). Such assistance may include detailing employees to the Conference to perform such functions consistent with the purposes of this order as the Conference may assign to them.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Department of Labor and the Department of Commerce shall ... furnish assistance to the Committee in accordance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945, 59 Stat. 134 (31 U.S.C. 691). Such assistance may include detailing employees to the Committee ... to perform such functions, consistent with the purposes of this order, as the Committee may assign to them.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive statutory-assistance machinery and sentence structure are closely reused, with the assisting agencies generalized for the Conference.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There is hereby established a conference ... The purpose of the Conference shall be ... improving existing administrative procedures. To this end the Conference shall conduct studies ... [and] report to the President ... together with suggestions for appropriate measures.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established the President's Advisory Committee ... The Committee shall study, and shall advise with and make recommendations to the President with respect to policies...
shared_material.explanation: Parallel opening sequence establishes the body and immediately assigns study and presidential-recommendation functions.
